name: Elafibranor
lead: Elafibranor (brand name Iqirvo; also GFT505) is an oral dual PPAR-alpha and PPAR-delta agonist developed by Genfit and marketed by Ipsen for primary biliary cholangitis (PBC).[1][2] The US FDA granted accelerated approval in June 2024, and the EU granted conditional authorization in September 2024.[1]

It is indicated with ursodeoxycholic acid in adults with an inadequate response, or alone in those who cannot tolerate it.[1] It had earlier been developed for nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), where a large phase 3 trial was terminated.[3][4] No studies of cosmetic, fat-loss or muscle outcomes were found; its relevance here is as a PPAR-delta-acting drug.

paras: The approved use is primary biliary cholangitis.[1][2] Wikipedia reports that Genfit is also studying it in type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.[1]
Wikipedia lists weight gain, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, joint pain, constipation, muscle injury, fracture, reflux, dry mouth, weight loss and rash among reported reactions.[1]

Elafibranor and its main active metabolite GFT1007 activate PPAR-alpha, PPAR-gamma and PPAR-delta in vitro.[1] A structural study compared its PPAR subtype preferences with seladelpar and lanifibranor.[5] Pharmacokinetic studies have been run in hepatic and renal impairment, elderly volunteers and Japanese participants.[6][7][8]

A phase 2 trial published in Gastroenterology in 2016 reported that elafibranor induced NASH resolution without fibrosis worsening in a subgroup analysis.[3] The phase 3 NASH study enrolled 2,157 patients and was terminated.[4] The FDA granted breakthrough therapy designation in 2019 on phase 2 PBC data, and the 2024 accelerated approval rested on the phase 3 ELATIVE trial.[1]

A phase 2 placebo-controlled trial in PBC with incomplete response to UDCA was published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2021.[9] The phase 3 ELATIVE trial was reported in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2024; Wikipedia gives a cholestasis response of 51 percent with elafibranor versus 4 percent with placebo at week 52.[10][1] The NASH program included the 2016 phase 2 study and a terminated phase 3 study.[3][4]
No studies found of elafibranor for appearance, fat loss or muscle goals.

timeline.event: Phase 2 NASH results published; phase 3 NASH trial begins.[3][4]

card.summary: An approved dual PPAR-alpha/delta agonist for primary biliary cholangitis, with no research on appearance or fat-loss outcomes.
card.note: Prescription liver drug under accelerated approval; NASH phase 3 trial was terminated.

quick.overview:
Elafibranor is a prescription drug approved in 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis. It activates two PPAR receptors, including PPAR-delta, which links it to fat-metabolism discussions.

Its trials track liver markers; none examine body composition or looks.
quick.mechanism: It and its main metabolite activate PPAR-alpha and PPAR-delta (and PPAR-gamma in vitro), receptors that regulate fat and bile acid metabolism.
quick.risks: Reported reactions include weight gain, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, joint pain, muscle injury and fracture, among others. It is prescription-only.
